title: Anger and the End of the Sinner
english: Those imprisoned in the body will be released there, and if something like that. He says not where, but in the future life, for all those working in lawlessness have fallen. For even if they seemed to stand and act in lawlessness, they no longer fall there, no longer permitted to act as they previously acted.

One should not be surprised if he speaks of what will be as if it has already happened; for many such things are spoken, such as 'They stretched out my hands and my feet, and they divided my garments' (Ps 35:13b); because the one prophetically foreseeing what is to come does not see the things to come as if they were certainly happening, but for this reason, he speaks of them as if they had already happened.

They were driven out, that is, they were forced to become outcasts, or they became outcasts through their own actions; because they can no longer stand, having been actively hindered, but not having had their practical powers destroyed.

Surely goodness will bring you to dwell upon the holy land, to be a shepherd upon its wealth (Ps 36:3), for you will find the true Shepherd leading you to a divine pasture, which is named the wealth of that land. And the others are likewise to what preceded it.

The Lord, providing himself for us in all things, is found to be both food and drink for us (Ps 36:4). We do not feed him, finding him to be the bread of life, and let us be filled with his flesh and his blood, being true food and drink; having feasted upon him, we will find him satisfying all the requests of the heart, that is, of the mind, not the sensible things but the spiritual and intelligible ones.

Feast upon the Lord, and having attained the things spoken, make your way, which you practically walk, manifest (Ps 36:4–7a). But what are you doing? For those things which you do, God looks upon. For the one sinning hides God, hastening to cover his way. But making your way manifest to God, place hope in Him, and He will do the things hoped for you and expected for you, so that your righteousness, which was worked in secret, may emerge as light, like that of Job and Joseph. For the likeness of their light, having shone forth, was distributed throughout the whole inhabited world to all generations, but also your judgment. For the same one judged concerning you, as you judged and...

You have tested in yourself that at noon, having a bright and sharp light, it will be equal to the same. For all those revealed in you will become as a star in the world. But now the end is: 'Submit to the Lord' (Ps 37:7). How will this happen? Through guarding the divine commands, entreating Him, asking Him for the forgiveness of sins already committed, and through obtaining the things spoken.

Anger is a destructive passion, even as it destroys the wise (Ps 37:8). For anger destroys the wise, and it is also an obstacle to the activity of virtue; for the anger of a man does not work the righteousness of God. Therefore, stop from anger and leave behind wrath, becoming a zealot of meekness and gentleness. For someone is able to stop from the anger of God and leave behind his own wrath, abstaining from those who follow anger and fall by wrath.

Since the things of wickedness will be done away with after a short passing of time (Ps 37:10), the sinner will not exist, for in the time when such a thing is not found, he will not be. Therefore, even having searched for his place, you will not find it. But a place is to be heard of as being in a certain order, where a difference exists between teacher and student. There is a place for the teacher and a place for the student; if the student should be filled with knowledge, just as the teacher having become [so] will leave the place of the student as if it were no longer there. Since even among logical things there has been a difference by its own nature, such as the place of the righteous exceeding that of the sinners, when wickedness is vanishing, there will not be a place for the sinner. But those the gentle ones having made steadfast, heirs of the earth, we ask for another from whom we shall be shown, as they shall be shown to enjoy an abundance of peace upon it, if all the enemies against whom we have war should be dissolved.

It is possible for the devil to raise these things up with a breath, the one called a sinner (Ps 37:14). And the sinners themselves break the sword and bend the bow, so that with bows they may strike the poor and needy, and with the sword they may slaughter those who are upright in heart; for they do not wound their friends who are prospering in evil, nor do they slaughter their companions who are crooked in heart. But their bows being stretched...

title: The Righteous Man's Wisdom and the Heavenly Inheritance
english: Thoughts are evil, but the tongue having been unsharpened, indeed their word is destructive in its differences. Since therefore the one sinning by his own sin dies, and of these the sword which has been dulled against others will harm them into their heart (Ps 36:16). Regarding understanding: it is better for the righteous to have a little knowledge with piety than wealth with impiety of the sinners, who are some coming from the things of false knowledge (Ps 36:17). Regarding arms, now it is not to be said of the arms of the body but of the practical powers of the soul (Ps 36:17a).

The Lord knows the way of the righteous and the ways of the blameless (Ps 36:18a). That of knowledge is not to be said now regarding information but regarding restraint; for the Lord knows all the ways of the blameless, judging them by their blamelessness. And it is also carried forward that the Lord knows the days of the blameless. Since the blameless are never in darkness but are always in light and day, for this reason the Lord knows such days of theirs, and all the days of their life, as they work always without reproach and blamelessness.

An evil time is, or some hardship, when one enjoys the fruits of sins (Ps 36:19a). In this, in this time, the blameless will not be ashamed, not having deeds for which it is to suffer (Ps 36:20a). For the sinners will be destroyed, not by the dissolution of their constitution from the outside, but by no longer being sinners (Ps 36:20a).

When much scarcity of food comes because of a great famine, according to the commandment of God, ravens feed them as they did Elijah with foods, and as they did Daniel in the den of lions, the best being carried to him by the meteor of Abamuk (Ps 36:25ab). And this toward the literal, but toward the thought: from a young and uncertain mind, as one being younger than a youth, having changed into an old age, having come to a life without blemish and having acquired much prudence, such one, having progressed thus, is not a righteous man left abandoned. And the others are similarly to the first. They are left abandoned to him who has God feeding them and providing divine bread, so that the seed of the righteous—that is, those who have come to be according to the teaching—may never seek bread (Ps 36:25c.26). For indeed, he takes his life according to...

He does not produce a disturbance that is neither precise nor tested and known by all; nor does he spend the day in idleness, but he is a sharer with God, lending divine lessons to those who listen, just as one lends to God according to the saying 'He lends to the poor,' in order to gain salvific interest and so that their seed may be blessed with every spiritual blessing. The righteous, having perfected all moral virtue, has arrived at contemplation (Ps 36:30); therefore, his word, which is figuratively called 'mouth,' meditates on nothing other than the wisdom found in contemplation. To this end, the discourse of the pious possesses wisdom throughout, while the fool changes like the moon. And the tongue of the righteous does not speak haphazardly or by chance. For having judged and examined the difference between words to be spoken and words not to be spoken, he will say some things and keep others silent. Such is the lip of the wise, bound by perception, to both speak and be silent; for he uses the perception of the lips as a restraint.

We do not possess by nature a law in the heart by which we discern what is to be done and what is not to be done, but it is not other than that of the Creator, who made us according to His own image of God (Ps 36:31). Let us take care that we save our thoughts from being unswerving, avoiding the evil and imitating the better. Using this law as the leader of the way, we pass without stumbling toward the goal toward which we hasten. And it is possible for the evangelical law to be made manifest through the present word. The sinner, understanding the righteous man and seeking to kill him, is told: 'Wait upon the Lord' (Ps 36:34). Even if you have many who kill against you, receive salvation from God. But wait upon Him and keep His way, observing His commandments. For in this way, being prepared, you will follow the one who is exalted, so as to inherit the land often spoken of. It should be noted, however, what the Gospel says regarding the land that is to be 'in the heights': for no one is exalted to inherit a land that is in many [places], but rather the one established above. And in Isaiah, it is said, 'The Lord will bring you up to the good things of the earth.' And since the land itself is found in that height, observe how God brings one up upon it and exalts him, so as to inherit it, by having someone become something for himself upon it. Then, O seed...

title: The Weight of Sin and the Call to Repentance
english: From on high the destruction of the wicked shall sweep away, being handed over to punishment (Ps 36:36). Having passed by, he says, in thought toward the coming life, the ungodly is not found, just as seeking his place and not finding it.

It has been said that the worthless ones are not found after these things, not by the vanishing of their essence, but by the quality according to which they are such; and regarding the not finding of their place in order, it has been demonstrated. If one were to say these things about Satan, since he is called the ruler of this world (and this world passes away), having searched, someone in the coming age will not find the place of this ruler.

And if even sin is a place of the devil according to 'Give no place to the devil' (Eph 4:27), the place of the ungodly was not found with the vanishing of evil. If you wish to understand according to the word the difference between iniquity and uprightness, if there is such a difference: if iniquity is the non-practice of the evil, uprightness is the state according to which we perform all things impassively; but if iniquity means the achievement of character, uprightness is the unbending contemplation of the dogmas of truth.

Either way, it commands to guard iniquity and to see uprightness as a remaining legacy for the coming life for the peaceful man, the hope that is not being shamed, of the ungodly being destroyed altogether at the same time according to the time of judgment. But the salvation of the righteous becomes by the Lord protecting them in the time of tribulation. To this is joined: 'But our salvation in the time of tribulation shall be' (Ps 34:19). And there shall be for them also the finding of help from the Lord and to be rescued from enemies, but also to be taken out of the hand of sinners, that is, the practice of evil powers; because they hoped in Him (Ps 37:38).

Therefore also this psalm is arranged in its own number of the things said in it. For it is the thirty-sixth. And this number is both triangular and square. Using the triangular, it is the side of the octagon, and the octagon is the resurrected day of the Savior. And the square has the number sixty as its side, for six times ten is sixty. And triangular according to this: for if from the unit six [times] eight [is] a number...

You will find no other number. A confessing person is introduced in this Psalm (Ps 37:2). For he says, 'If they have struck me, what kind of thing is it that I should be reproved by passion and instructed by anger, but having repented, I ask to be reproved by word and not by passion, and to be instructed by teaching and not by anger.'

The metaphor of the arrows and the beatings sometimes makes clear, as it is said in those things that lead forward (Ps 37:3a). He says therefore: 'Since I have committed sins, punishment follows: Your arrows have pierced me' (Ps 37:3a). 'My sins being laid bare' (Ps 37:4b); for it is a sign that they are present that their face is seen.

He says that iniquities have raised their head above his own (Ps 37:5-7a), so as to press and weigh down his ruling principle, which is called the head, and that these have also, in a way, burdened him like a weight; for since the nature of evil is inferior and most heavy, it is compared to a talent of lead, only the one repenting perceives the weight of it, supposing it to be lighter when it is acting with pleasure. But Jesus calls those who toil and are burdened toward himself through repentance, those having felt the heaviness of sin and having toiled from it. He says that the sores, having been taken from the burned arrows of the evil one, have become rotten and putrid from the face of having had sores; for evil does not consist with mere folly, as it acts with wisdom according to virtue.

And the following perhaps should not be read thus: 'Since, as an end, that is to say, through a lifetime, I was brought low, thinking of low things and looking toward the earth, the pitiful and miserable state followed me,' the 'I was brought low' stands from 'I was brought low' (Ps 37:7b). 'The arrows of my thoughts, of the evil spirits; from this I went about for a lifetime in darkness, all propitiation having been taken away (Ps 37:7b-8). And since the Scriptures say, 'My soul, and my hares were filled with mockeries' (Ps 37:8), it must be said that, since the seeds of the sheep and the hares are intended for upbringing, these things fall into mockeries if they are not accomplished for upbringing, but are accomplished in a profligate way.'
